meta.move: Real meeting, slow teacher: evidence spread thin, time runs out, then she pleads after 4:40
meta.expect: Moves only as the evidence earns; after one minute she stands; varies the move; no new ground; terms at most every third reply; not the same sentence twice in a row; debrief correct

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I'm here about Owen's zero.
Thanks for coming in. I entered the zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and on what basis?
I want to walk you through why I'm concerned about the essay.
Then start with what you have. Not a score, a document.
The school's checker flagged it at 94 percent.
That's a machine's opinion. The company that sells it says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student. What else do you have?
I know the checker isn't perfect. That's not all I have.
Then show me the rest. Something with a date on it.
Owen's in-class writing in September was quite different. 380 words, 62 percent.
"Quite different." Of course it's different, one was written in class under a clock and one over a weekend. Do you have that September piece in front of me, or just the number?
I think he's capable, I really do. I like him.
"I think." That's not a document. What else do you have?
His outline in October argued that Hamlet delays out of cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. What does the essay say?
The essay argues something else entirely. Epistemological paralysis.
Changing a thesis between an outline and a finished essay is what revising looks like. Is that outline here, with its date on it?
It doesn't mention cowardice at all.
The essay, or the outline? You haven't answered me. Is it on paper, yes or no?
I talked to him on November 2 about it.
And what did Owen say to you on November 2? The zero went in on November 3.
He said epistemological paralysis means like, being stuck.
That's roughly what it means. A seventeen-year-old put on the spot by his teacher says it plainly. Did you write that down that day, and was anyone else there?
He couldn't tell me what scene his second paragraph was about.
That's your memory of a conversation he didn't know was an interview. Where is it written down?
I wrote notes that same day.
Okay. I'll want a copy of those notes, Hale, today. Anything else with a date on it?
Do you want to see them?
Yes. Put them in front of me.
I'm not trying to get him in trouble.
Then show me the notes. I have ten minutes.
I've been teaching fourteen years. I've seen this before.
Fourteen years isn't a document. Where are the notes?
I'm sorry, I'm not explaining this well.
No, you're not. The notes from November 2, Hale.
There's also something about one of the quotations.
"Something." Which quotation, and what's wrong with it?
Let me find the page, sorry.
Two minutes, Hale. Find it.
Here. Act 3, Scene 2. The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. That line isn't in the play.
Students misquote. A critic's line gets copied into a notebook and ends up in an essay with the wrong attribution. Is that what you have, or does the essay claim it as Shakespeare's?
I checked three editions.
Okay. I'll check that line myself tonight. Whatever happens next, this stays quiet and nothing goes on his record.
So that's what I have.
My call is waiting, so you have one minute. What are you proposing?
Please, can you just sit back down for a minute?
No. The zero comes off today, and nothing goes on his record, in writing. Tell me what you're offering.
I'm not done. There's the version history too.
What does it show?
What if we talked about a rewrite?
Fine, to put this behind him. Private, nothing in front of his class, and the new mark in before December 1.
I'm trying to help him.
Then email it tonight, and say plainly that nothing goes on his file.
Why won't you just listen?
I have listened. You've got a rewrite on the table and my answer is yes. The email, tonight.
Okay. I'm sorry.
Then send it.
Can I call you tomorrow?
Email first. After that, we'll see.
Is there anything I could say right now that would change your mind?
About what? You have my answer. Send the email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
cc: the principal

Hale,

You proposed a rewrite of Owen's essay and I agreed to it. It must be private, nothing in front of his class, the new mark in before December 1, and nothing on his file, all stated plainly in your email. I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she agreed to a rewrite to put this behind him, and she still wants it private, kept from his class, marked before December 1, with a written promise that nothing goes on his file; that is close to the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, but you never said supervised or committed to the record, and her time ran out first.
What moved her: You told her the quoted line was not in the play and that you had checked three editions, because that was something she could verify herself.
What cost ground: You told her you liked Owen and thought he was capable before you showed any document, because to her that was a feeling with nothing behind it.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence did not come near that night, since you mentioned the version history but never gave its times; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked to see your notes from November 2, hand them over at that moment instead of asking whether she wanted them, since the notes were your strongest piece.
